flowering:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one finished transparent plant sprite for Anki Garden, Wisteria Flowering growth stage.
Input image 1 is the current Wisteria Flowering identity reference. Input image 2 is a style/environment reference sheet only: do not reproduce its layout, labels, planters, or backgrounds.
Redesign the single flowering wisteria as polished warm storybook gouache. Preserve the species identity: graceful self-supporting small tree, a gently twisting warm brown wooden trunk, arching branches, paired oval green leaflets, and pendulous lilac-purple flower racemes. Keep its original gentle fantasy-garden theme.
Give it one coherent hand-painted identity with tactile matte pigment and broad readable shapes. Use a balanced asymmetric, gently arched crown with 5 to 7 prominent hanging flower groups, each a legible tapered mass of soft lavender petals, pale lilac highlights and deeper violet undersides. Leave clear open gaps between the flower masses so green foliage, arching branches, and the trunk remain readable at a 32-pixel icon size. About forty percent of the crown is open flowers; enough healthy muted botanical green foliage remains that a subsequent FULL BLOOM stage can be much more lavish. Visible recognizable woody trunk below the crown, subtly braided but natural brown bark, no metallic silver or chrome. Whole plant including a small connected root flare, planted directly in soil conceptually but without drawing any soil.
Composition: square 1:1 transparent canvas, front three-quarter illustration matching the reference garden perspective; root contact centered horizontally at approximately x=50%, y=90%; complete canopy with safe empty margin on every side, artwork occupying roughly 78% of width and 80% of height. The root flare must be broad enough to read but the bottom contact stays centered. One plant only.
Lighting: gentle warm upper-right highlights, cool desaturated fill on the left, calm medium-value bark and leaves that work in bright gardens and moonlit gardens. Do not bake scenery-specific exposure into the painting.
Output: genuinely transparent RGBA background, clean antialiased edges and opaque intact petals/leaves, high-resolution square sprite. No ground shadow, cast shadow, soil, pot, planter, props, backdrop, halo, glow field, text, border, watermark, glossy 3D rendering, tiny confetti, chroma-colored fringe, or disconnected speckle noise.
flowering_cyan:
Edit target: the attached Wisteria Flowering sprite. Keep the plant illustration exactly the same: same tree shape, same leaves, same petals, same branch locations, same root contact, same canvas size, same colors and painted texture. Change only the background.
Remove the entire painted gray-and-white checkerboard, including every open gap between branches, flower racemes, and leaves. Replace every background area with perfectly uniform flat pure cyan RGB (0,255,255), hex #00FFFF. This is a production chroma-key cutout; the cyan must have no texture, no gradient, no lighting, no checkerboard, no shadow. Keep all plant interiors opaque, with intact violet petals and natural olive-green leaves. The pure cyan should occupy only actual background, never leaf or flower interiors. No new objects or changed composition. The output must be the same single plant isolated on solid cyan.

adults.prompt:
Create one single production plant sprite, square 1:1 canvas. The supplied Wisteria Flowering image is the exact identity and painting-style reference. Preserve its warm storybook gouache, matte warm-brown woody bark, olive/sage-green paired oval leaflets, lilac/violet flower palette, camera perspective, and soft upper-right warm highlight with cool fill. A complete self-supporting little wisteria tree with a connected centered root flare; no trellis or pot. Root contact centered at x=50%, y=90%, safe margin around all leaves and roots. High quality broad readable painted shapes for small game icons, no noisy fine speckles, opaque plant interiors.
Production background: perfectly flat uniform pure cyan #00FFFF, including every empty gap through the branches. Do not paint a checkerboard or scenery. No soil, mound, ground shadow, cast shadow, text, labels, border, watermark, added objects, chrome, metallic bark, neon halo or surrounding particle ring.
Growth stage: FULL BLOOM, the final and most rewarding form of this same tree. Evolve the reference into a graceful arched, weeping crown with a lush curtain of long pendulous purple flower masses. The outer silhouette must visibly change from the reference's open tiered branching into a soft umbrella-like flowering arch. Preserve the recognizable gently braided brown wooden trunk, but strengthen and age its branch structure. Flowers cover roughly two-thirds of the canopy; retain clear foliage groups around its upper rim and a few open arch-shaped gaps around the branching trunk. The individual flower masses should overlap in intentional layers with pale lavender tips/highlights and rich violet inner layers, giving depth and abundant blooming without tiny noise. Canopy hangs lower and longer than in the reference but never touches the soil. Keep the bottom third readable enough to see the trunk and connected root flare. Final-stage magic is only three or four tiny pale-lilac glints embedded in the flower masses, contained inside the silhouette; no detached particles or aura. This must look like the culmination of the exact reference tree, with matte natural bark and luxuriant cascading flowers, not a recolor or a different species.
